notes: L1 regression suite: real obfuscated .so files the decompiler does not
control the source of, unlike eval/ which is built from known C. There is
no ground truth here, so a case is scored on structural shape only --
goto/switch/ternary counts and a clean (exit 0) decompile -- not on the
signature or type checks eval/manifest.json can make.

cases.name: sample_jni_onload
cases.comment: OLLVM-flattened JNI_OnLoad: a state variable (named 'state', see analysis/variables.cpp's dispatcher-state promotion) is threaded through if-chains and a table load (g_1e14d0 base + state*8) that picks the next block. Before boundOnIndex learned to read a branchless clamp (a select whose own condition, or whose arm's own width, proves it -- see analysis/index_bound.cpp's localBound/armBound), 15 of this table's 16 targets stayed unresolved: only the state transitions a *branch* happened to guard were provable, so most of the state machine was invisible and the metrics below looked deceptively small. All 16 branches now resolve -- verified by hand against the raw g_1e14d0 bytes, every one matches -- so the shape below is the whole real state machine: 4 switches (one per place a clamped state selects the next block), 16 labelled blocks, and the goto/undef counts that come from copying live registers across every one of those edges. That copying (a case's t8..t15 = a0..a7 chain, mostly /*undef*/ because a state transition rarely uses all eight) is exactly what Phase 1a/1b's dispatcher-loop structurizer exists to fold into a single 'while(state) switch(state)' with real variables instead of a labelled goto per edge -- shrinking this further is that work, not a fix to this analysis.

cases.name: sample_mega_dispatcher
cases.comment: Not actually a mega dispatcher: this is a small 4-way syscall helper (gettimeofday, by its shape) whose CFG the lifter used to bleed into hundreds of unrelated blocks two different ways -- 'bl __stack_chk_fail@plt' was scanned as a returning call instead of ending the block (see analysis/noreturn.h), and a branchless clamp ('cmp x, #3; csel x, replacement, x, gt') that bounds one of its four indirect-branch indices was invisible to boundOnIndex, so the enumerator fell back to reading hundreds of table slots as if the index were unbounded. Fixing both drops this from 320 blocks / ~97k lines to the real function: 7 blocks, a 3-way switch, a stack-canary check that correctly ends in __builtin_unreachable(), and a clean return. The thresholds below are pinned close to that shape on purpose -- this case exists specifically to catch either bleed-through or bound over-estimation coming back.

cases.name: sample_core_mba
cases.comment: L2: a real, unmodified app's core algorithm entry -- a straight-line MBA block of ~5400 IL ops with no internal branch (the round-1 lifted shape), dispatched into ~163 more such blocks by a byte-indexed jump table once the driver resolves it over several rounds. Registered per the mega-block local-simplify fix (see eval/FINDINGS.md's 2026-08-10 note): before that fix, decompiling this address hung indefinitely in copyPropagateBlock/dceBlock's unbounded expression-tree growth and never produced output at all, so 'exits 0 within the round budget' is itself most of what this case is guarding. --allow-unresolved is defensive -- at the default round budget every branch this dispatcher has resolves cleanly, but a lower round cap would not finish resolving before hitting the driver's cap. Per the 2026-08-10 dispatcher-handler-inlining fix (see eval/FINDINGS.md): 161 of the 162 cases share one tail block (restore live registers, jump back to the dispatch loop) that analysis::matchDispatcherShape now recognises, so the structurizer inlines each case up to that shared tail (see structure.cpp's claimDispatcherCaseBody) and prints the tail once as the switch's own epilogue instead of once per case. Per the Live Register Frame plan (F0-F4, same FINDINGS.md date): the ~1200 lines of `tN = tM` noise in that tail turned out to be phi edge copies relaying x0-x7 through the merge block's own second phi site, not a real x0-x7/x8-x15 shadow bank -- analysis/live_register_frame.h models that relay directly, and c_stmt.cpp's printEdge uses it to print a handler's save copy only where classifyHandlerExit says the handler actually changed something (a one-time seed ahead of the switch establishes the invariant that makes skipping the rest safe). F4 then extended tryDispatcherLoop to recognise the guard's own out-of-range arm as one more private handler feeding the same merge block (exactly what put it inside the natural loop's own block set in the first place, tripping the older 'genuine exit' assumption) and inline it as the loop's `if`/`else` rather than a label outside it. That closes the three-way convergence noted below: goto count is now 0 and the whole function is one `while (true)`. The thresholds below keep light slack over that shape, not a target -- tighten them (and samples/baseline.json via -UpdateBaseline) per samples/README.md's 'increment slowly' rule.

cases.name: sample_afRDLog
cases.comment: L2: a real, unmodified app's largest OLLVM-flattened JNI function (afRDLog @ its ELF symbol, [0x841ac, 0x93e98), 724/724 lifted PCs inside the symbol -- the boundary is correct, see eval/FINDINGS.md for why the nearby 0x627ac is not a usable entry instead). Registered per the bc_lib OLLVM optimization plan as the L2 gate every phase of that plan is measured against; there is no ground truth here, only shape. Phases 0-5 of that plan have landed (state slot ID, undef-copy coalescing, hub/switch structuring, the cancelled-subtrahend and declaration-grouping readability passes, and the driver's discovery hard cap); see eval/FINDINGS.md for the per-phase before/after. The thresholds below are the 2026-08 post-phase-5 shape with light slack, not a target -- tighten them (and samples/baseline.json via -UpdateBaseline) as further work lands, per samples/README.md's 'increment slowly' rule.

cases.name: sample_libscplugin
cases.comment: L2: a real app's large OLLVM-flattened function, registered per docs/18-architecture-optimization-plan.md as an observational, non-blocking regression guard. Before the resolved-binary-dispatch collapse (see structure.cpp's switchFor and analysis::matchDispatchValues), every one of this function's 244 table-mode switches turned out to be exactly two-way -- an obfuscator's original `if` reaching its two arms through a shared jump table once value-set analysis narrows the table to the two live entries a preceding select's own two constants produce. Recognising that shape and printing `if (cond) A else B` instead of a numbered two-case switch took switches from 244 to 0 and loops (while(true)) from 5 to 43. J1 (docs/18's §5.2, structure.cpp's StructureOptions::minRegionSites) then deferred that collapse specifically for this function's one 234-site analysis::DispatchRegion (sharedTail=false, so nothing else consumes it yet) -- switches went back to 234 (matching this table's original shape almost exactly) and, as a direct consequence, the if-chain-driven loop recognition that had produced 43 while(true) wrappers no longer fires on these now-uncollapsed sites, dropping loops_while_true to 2. docs/19-scatter-dispatch-target-shape.md then verified, from the assembly rather than assumed, that this region's own sharedTail=false is exactly the scatter shape J1's defer was never meant to protect (that machinery is for the shared-tail flattened-loop shape instead) -- the region-membership half of J1's defer now only ever protects a region that actually votes a sharedTail, so a sharedTail-less region like this one always collapses, and switches go from 234 to 0 again, this time as 533 nested if/else-if (a 93-root, 28-deep decision forest, see the CLI's own `--emit-report` dispatch-nest diagnostic), not the flat if/else the pre-J1 shape had before this region was even recognised as one. gotos rose 289 -> 332 -- the if/else-if collapse does not (yet) build the table-mode switch's own shared-epilogue-for-a-multi-tail-hub shape, so a hub several sites share costs one goto per site instead of one shared inline; docs/19 §4 records this as an accepted, not-yet-closed gap, not a defect. The goto-elimination plan (docs/19's own follow-up) then closed part of that gap: Phase 1 gave `If` the same join-hub epilogue Switch already had, Phase 2's `restructureSkipGotos` unwound the `if (cond) goto M; else {WORK}` shape switchFor's unbounded arm walk otherwise leaves behind, taking gotos 332 -> 303; Phase 3 then widened `deadRoutingStateStore`'s own paired-if shape (c_stmt.cpp) to trust an arm Phase 1/2 inlined in place of a bare goto, not only a bare goto itself, dropping the `state=select(cond,...)` duplicate stores those inlined arms had been keeping alive and taking ifs from above 500 down to 386. Phase 4's `simplifyGuardedSpins` then caught `wrapAsLoop`'s own `while (true) { if (cond) { continue; } else { WORK } }` remnants -- exactly the shape `tryLoop`'s `CondBranch` match never gets a chance to see once Phase 0's collapse has already turned the header into a 2-way `If` -- and rewrote each into the plain `while (cond) { }` it already meant, splicing `WORK` in right after: loops_while_true 49 -> 12, gotos 303 -> 273 (Phase 2's own elision catches a fresh fallthrough the splice exposes at several of those sites), ifs 386 -> 349. The thresholds below are this shape with light slack -- tighten them (and samples/baseline.json via -UpdateBaseline) as the epilogue gap closes further, per samples/README.md's 'increment slowly' rule.

cases.name: sample_sub_b7000
cases.comment: L2: a small scatter-dispatcher function from the same OLLVM-flattened binary as sample_libscplugin above, registered per the goto-elimination plan (docs/architecture-optimization-eval-prompt.md) as its own fast-to-decompile regression guard -- small enough to eyeball the whole emitted C by hand after every phase, unlike its mega-function sibling. It is exactly the null-check-chain + property-loop shape the plan's own worked examples (sub_b7000_collapse.c) are drawn from: Phase 0's always-on scatter collapse first turns its ~93-root dispatch forest from table-mode switches into nested if/else-if, landing at 26 gotos; Phase 1's join-hub epilogue for `If` (mirroring the one `Switch` already had) and Phase 2's `restructureSkipGotos` (unwinding the `if (cond) goto M; else {WORK}` shape switchFor's own arm walk otherwise leaves behind) together take that to 20; Phase 3's widened `deadRoutingStateStore` (c_stmt.cpp) drops the redundant `state=select(cond,...)` stores those inlined arms leave duplicated behind, taking ifs from ~40 to 31 without moving gotos; Phase 4's `simplifyGuardedSpins` then catches the `while (true) { if (cond) { continue; } else { WORK } }` remnant `wrapAsLoop` leaves once Phase 0 has already turned a loop's own header into a 2-way `If`, rewriting it into the plain `while (cond) {}` it always meant and taking gotos 20 -> 19, ifs 31 -> 30. Phase 5's own `If`-arm orphan fold (expandGotoTargets, structure.cpp) found nothing left to claim here -- this function's residual gotos all turn out to be genuine multi-reference hubs, not orphans a traversal order merely stranded -- so the shape stayed exactly there. The thresholds below are that shape with light slack, not a target -- tighten them (and samples/baseline.json via -UpdateBaseline) as later phases close more of the gap, per samples/README.md's 'increment slowly' rule.

cases.name: sample_absd_start
cases.comment: L2: the first Mach-O/iOS case, registered per the iOS Mach-O support plan -- a real, unmodified iOS binary's LC_MAIN entry point, `start()`. Originally bounded to one round to hold just the *entry*, decompiled correctly, without the flattened state machine behind its first dispatch (see eval/FINDINGS.md's Tier A entry for the numbers at higher round counts pre-dating this note). It stacks three obfuscation layers the pseudocode this case was designed against shows directly: a stack-canary-derived index (`__stack_chk_guard` XORed/multiplied with a value derived from the stack pointer) into `off_1000A2A10`, a mixed table of rebase-resolved internal function pointers and bind-resolved named imports (`_mach_msg`, `_malloc`, `_sscanf`, ...) that macho.cpp's dyld rebase/bind opcode interpreter (Phase 2 of that plan) makes concrete; a global write through a pointer stored in `__DATA_CONST` rather than a fixed address (resolves to exactly `g_1000a8140`, matching the pseudocode's `dword_1000A8140`, which needs that segment recorded read-only -- dyld write-protects it once its fixups are applied, whatever initprot says); and a final `BR X9` computed jump whose target is the *return value* of the first indirect call -- a call whose own callee is only known at runtime (it is selected by the stack canary, which dyld/the kernel randomises per process), so the jump is genuinely, not just budget-limited, unresolvable by static analysis alone. 2026-08-14 (absd 间接跳转全解析优化计划, Phase 3): the driver's intra-round settle loop (driver.cpp, `kSettleCeiling`) now keeps lifting and re-probing within a *single* round for as long as it keeps discovering, so `--rounds 1` no longer bounds this case to the entry's own first dispatch the way the comment above once assumed -- one round settles as deep into the chain of small dispatchers as `sample_absd_start_chain` (cap 36) does, converging on the identical shape. That is a direct, accepted consequence of the fix that closed absd's 9a4 site (see that case's own comment): the driver has no way to tell 'still opening the level a round is already on' apart from 'the next level of the chain' when both look like the same thing, a not-yet-lifted discovery. The thresholds below are that converged shape with slack, not a target -- tighten via samples/README.md's 'increment slowly' rule if the settle loop is ever bounded to preserve a true one-round wall.

cases.name: sample_absd_start_chain
cases.comment: L2, one step further than sample_absd_start: discovery-cap 36 is still below the real ~40-target dispatcher's cliff (raising it to 40 still reproduces sample_absd_start_l2's ~11500-line explosion, confirmed 2026-08-14), so everything this case admits is the chain of small dispatchers *leading up to* that one real fan-out, not the fan-out itself. Before this fix that chain did not resolve either, for a reason with nothing to do with the cap: 0x1000234b0 and 0x1000234f8 each compute their index from two arithmetic terms that are individually a single bit read twice, not two -- `shr.u(x,31)` next to `shr.u(not(x),31)` at the first site, `!(a==b)` next to `!(a!=b)` at the second. preciseIndexSet (analysis/index_bound.h) used to resolve each term on its own, which invents the two combinations where both bits agree (impossible -- they are the same bit) alongside the two where they legitimately disagree, so a 1-bit question came out as 2 bits' worth of candidates: 308 and 295 respectively, both hopeless under any cap that keeps the rest of this function finite. Recognising the pair as one shared bit (see index_bound.cpp's BitFactor) collapses them to their true 2 and 4, small enough for resolve_indirect's discovery cap to admit and its `switch (index)` emission (sample_absd_start's case) to render structurally -- four real dispatch sites, not one opaque region. The forbidden pattern is that failure's shape: an address-relative switch discriminant is what a dispatcher falls back to the moment its table stops being recognisable behind a phi resolve_indirect could not resolve at all. 2026-08-14 (absd 间接跳转全解析优化计划): four more phases closed two of the four sites this case used to seal (688/938/9a4/8dc). ImageEval's phi/select union now drops a stale EntryReg arm sitting next to an arm that actually redefines the same register (image_eval.cpp's unionEntryRegAware) instead of merging the two; preciseIndexSet gained cinc/csinc's `select(cond, state+1, state)` shape, an OR-chain walk that finds a complementary cset pair past intervening nesting, and -- the fix that actually closed 938 -- a `Value` case that reads through a loop-carried phi's own arms (a dispatcher state register, absd's reg:x9/x10/x11) the same way ImageEval already did, rather than stopping at the `val:iN(%k)` wrapper and calling it unknown; the driver now settles a chain of indirect branches within one round instead of needing an extra round per hop; and LC_DYLD_CHAINED_FIXUPS decoding (macho.cpp) means a companion dyld image's own rebase/bind slots read as real pointers instead of raw chain words. `0x100023938` and `0x1000239a4` (the entries needing a resolved dyld pointer and a same-round lift respectively) are gone from this run's output as a direct result -- but only when the local absd copy has a `dyld` companion (`dyld` file next to it, or an `absd.entry.json` sidecar naming one; docs/21-entry-reg-platform.md) as this case's own local.json binary now does. Without one, x22 stays top and both of those sites seal again exactly as before -- not a regression, the same graceful degrade the sidecar mechanism always had. `0x100023688` and `0x1000238dc` remain sealed for reasons neither phase addresses: `0x100023688`'s cinc index is `select(cond, entry:x22, entry:x22+1)` with *no* other write to x22 anywhere in this run's reachable CFG at all -- ImageEval resolves it to a concrete pair of huge, correctly-rejected-as-not-code offsets, so this is not a missing fact but either a genuinely unreachable dispatch state or a predecessor block this round budget never discovers; `0x1000238dc`'s index folds in a value that traces back through a phi to `%189`, an actual argument this function receives, with no guard on this path bounding it -- correctly beyond what a structural, non-argument-range analysis can claim. Lines/gotos/undef all grew with the two newly-resolved sites (more real code rendered instead of one opaque stub each), so those thresholds moved up with them; unresolved_branches tightened from 6 to the 2 now provably left.

cases.name: sample_absd_start_l2
cases.comment: L2: the same iOS entry as sample_absd_start, meant to let the flattened state machine behind its first dispatch actually open -- four rounds and a per-branch discovery cap of 64 (see driver.h's DriverOptions::maxDiscoveryPerBranch). Observational, like sample_libscplugin: the thresholds are a measured shape with slack, not a target. Originally (2026-08-13) that cap was what took the output from ~117 lines to ~10800 by admitting a ~40-target dispatcher whole. 2026-08-14 (absd 间接跳转全解析优化计划): after Phase 1-4's precision fixes (see sample_absd_start_chain's comment) plus Phase 3's intra-round settling, this run no longer reaches that 40-target dispatcher at all -- it converges on the exact same shape sample_absd_start_chain (cap 36) and sample_absd_start (rounds 1) do, one round's settle loop already exhausting everything the extra rounds and the wider cap here used to be needed for. Which upstream change removed the path that used to reach it has not been root-caused; the two most direct suspects are Phase 1a's EntryReg filtering (image_eval.cpp's unionEntryRegAware) removing a union arm that used to feed a wider, if imprecise, candidate set, or the phi-following addition to exactValues (index_bound.cpp) resolving some intermediate branch to a narrower set than it used to fall back to. Kept as a regression guard for that direction (the cap and round count stay higher than the other two cases in case a future fix reopens a deeper path); the fan-out itself remains unreached and its correctness at the old 40-target shape was never independently verified either way.
